Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

quamvīs

conjunction, with the subjunctive in classical prose; with an adjective or adverb, “however”

although, however much; despite (being), however (much); even if, however much; however (much), however + adjective

In this lexicon

  • although

    also used · classical · Ov. Met. 6.376: quamvīs sint sub aquā, sub aquā maledīcere temptant; Cic. Tusc. 2.13: ager quamvīs fertilis

  • despite

    the recommended word · classical · Mart. 13.81.1: quamvīs lāta gerat patella rhombum; Plin. NH 9.25: quamvīs occultus atque abditus

  • even if

    also used · classical · Ov. Rem. 213–214: tū tantum quamvīs firmīs retinēbere vinclīs, ī procul

  • however

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Tusc. 2.13: ager quamvīs fertilis; Cic. Sen. 67: quamvīs sit adulēscēns; Mart. 13.81.1

Examples

  • quamvīs sint sub aquā, sub aquā maledīcere temptant

    though they are under water, under water they try to curseOv. Met. 6.376

    In the entry for although

  • ego etsī nihil habeō quod ad tē scrībam, scrībō tamen quia tēcum loquī videor

    even though I have nothing to write to you, I write all the same, because I feel I am talking with youCic. Att. 12.53.1

    In the entry for despite

  • quamvīs lāta gerat patella rhombum, rhombus lātior est tamen patellā

    however wide the dish that holds the turbot, the turbot is wider than the dishMart. 13.81.1–2

    In the entry for despite

  • quamvīs sint sub aquā, sub aquā maledīcere temptant

    though they are under water, under water they still try to curseOv. Met. 6.376

    In the entry for despite

  • ut ager quamvīs fertilis sine cultūrā frūctuōsus esse nōn potest, sīc sine doctrīnā animus

    as a field, however fertile, cannot bear fruit without tilling, so neither can a mind without teachingCic. Tusc. 2.13

    In the entry for despite

  • etenim ille, quoniam semel indūxit animum sibi licēre quod vellet, fēcisset nihilō minus mē invītō

    for once he had made up his mind that he could do as he liked, he would have done it all the same, despite meCic. Att. 14.13.6

    In the entry for despite

  • Rapere est, nōn petere, quidquid invītō auferās.

    Whatever you take from someone against his will is grabbing, not asking.Publil. Sent. R 26

    In the entry for despite

  • tū tantum quamvīs firmīs retinēbere vinclīs, ī procul, et longās carpere perge viās

    only, even if strong ties hold you back, go far away, and set out on long roadsOv. Rem. 213–214

    In the entry for even if

    however wide the dish that holds the turbot, the turbot is wider than the dishMart. 13.81

    In the entry for however

  • utcumque erit, juvābit tamen

    however it turns out, I shall still be glad of itLiv. praef. 3

    In the entry for however

    however you can, make sure you come to meCic. Fam. 14.4.3
